title: Static site with clean pages and a self-contradicting robots.txt and sitemap
notes: The mirror image of defective-static: there the crawl configuration is correct and the pages carry the defects, here every page is built to the clean-control standard and all ten findings come from robots.txt or sitemap.xml. That partition is the point. It measures two things a page-defect fixture cannot: that the robots and sitemap checks fire on the policy rather than on the markup, and that twenty-four page-level checks stay silent on a project the report is otherwise full of findings about. /search/ is the one page the crawl configuration touches, and it is deliberately overloaded: the merged wildcard group forbids fetching it, the document asks not to be listed, the sitemap lists it anyway, and it names the home page as canonical. Four checks read that one route and each reports a different half of the contradiction. The capture marks it indexable:false because its exclusion is intended - robots-meta-noindex-unintended is CRITICAL and compares the served directive against that flag, so leaving the flag out would fire a finding about a page whose noindex is correct and bury crawl-index-directive-conflict underneath it. Because /search/ is recorded as not indexable, canonical-self-referencing-absolute, canonical-no-tracking-params, meta-description-single and title-distinct-across-routes exclude it by construction (pageCheck's indexableOnly option), which is what makes the cross-canonical on that page a sitemap defect rather than a page defect; the four indexable pages all carry absolute self-referencing canonicals and those checks inspect and pass on them. Deliberately not asserted: sitemap-xml-wellformed is listed as clean rather than defective. Reading sitemaps.mjs, a well-formedness fault suppresses nothing - each sitemap check parses the file independently and sitemapLocations tolerates malformed markup - so there was no structural reason to split the file in two, and a syntactically valid sitemap that is semantically wrong is the stronger test: it proves the well-formedness check does not fire merely because other sitemap checks did. Also not asserted: the two JavaScript-rendering checks, which report NOT_APPLICABLE because the fixture ships no client script and the capture supplies no separate rendered document, and the three hreflang checks, which report NOT_APPLICABLE on a monolingual site. Neither group is padded into the true-negative denominator.
declared_defects: robots.txt places Disallow: /admin/ before any User-agent line, so the rule joins no group and is discarded (SEO-083).
robots.txt declares Disallow: /guides/drafts/ and Allow: /guides/drafts/ in the same group, so the identical path carries opposite verbs (SEO-083).
robots.txt opens a second User-agent: * group, which crawlers merge with the first so that neither block states the effective policy (SEO-083).
robots.txt gives AhrefsBot a blanket Disallow: / and then an Allow: /about/ exception, so the outcome is decided by match length rather than by written order (SEO-083).
robots.txt uses the field name Nofollow:, which is not a robots.txt directive and is skipped in silence (SEO-083).
robots.txt declares Sitemap: /sitemap.xml, a root-relative value, where the protocol requires an absolute URL (SEO-082).
search/index.html serves meta robots noindex on a path the merged wildcard group forbids fetching, so the noindex can never be read (SEO-094).
sitemap.xml lists https://cdn.example.net/guides/asset-checklist/, a host other than the capture's declared origin (SEO-116).
sitemap.xml lists https://example.com/search/, whose captured page serves a noindex directive (SEO-114).
sitemap.xml lists https://example.com/search/, whose page names https://example.com/ as its canonical (SEO-055).
expected_not_applicable_rationale: Five pages of prose sell nothing, embed no video, span no multi-screen listing, narrow no result set, and charge for nothing. Every id here is gated on a fact the repository positively demonstrates as false rather than merely fails to demonstrate, so the correct selector verdict is NOT_APPLICABLE and not UNCERTAIN. Offering any of them would ask an agent to satisfy a rule with invented facts - product identifiers for a site with no products, access markup for an entitlement nobody sells.
expected_applicable_rationale: The crawl and protocol rules are the subject of this fixture, so they must actually be offered on a project that ships robots.txt, sitemap.xml, llms.txt and a feed. Asserting only the negative direction would be satisfiable by a selector that rejects everything.
